text:
role models come in two kinds

one is books, the other is people.

books are objectively are going to be the best choice as far as how to think about principles, virtues and vices, weights and values, who u want to model yourself after, and so on.

(1/5) 

who are you supposed to choose? 

any human that has ever lived over the last 2000+ years

why do it this way?

because this is simply how it is done, homeboy. each book shows u how they did it. Napoleon didn't want to be Davout or Ney, he wanted to be Caesar, and Caesar, in turn wanted to be Alexander, and Alexander wanted to be Achilles.

2000+ years separate those men. this is just how it goes.

whereas in person, u arent choosing from every human ever.

(2/5) 

here, u are plopped into some group of like, 4 family members, some friends, maybe u meet 1,000 people in the years to come. 

it could be 10,000, it doesn't matter.

there's 8 billion people right now.

then, run that back over 2000 years.

the chance that u randomly spawned, here and now, with the next Winston Churchill.....are probably .000000001%.

it's okay to love your family, brothers, seniors, mentors, and all of that, and respect and admire them.  and u can also have role models in strange places, u can have Plutarch, Montaigne, Tom Brady, and some random guy on Twitter who u have DM'ed with for 15 years, know of one another, but have never met in person.

but in real life, just be aware you're clouded by emotion and youth and a life in progress, as are they, and also keep in mind that no one you know has any fucking clue what they're doing.

it's a staircase where at 25, the 35 year old guy is wise. then you get to 35 and realize you're dumb a bag of hammers. it's false idols all the way down.

3/5

here is how it works. there's something to be said for death in "clearing the decks" and allowing you full inspection of a man.

a man in his 40's and 50's is often a puppet, being pulled by several strings and pulleys and levers which are not always conducive to being a good role model.

There's tradeoffs being made constantly and the notion of society being a moral place is almost comedic, which has been a constant for the past 2000 years.

most men are two men, you saw the public, you'll see the private, and you'll figure it out.

but that's why u can't really be worshipping a man who is still writing his story, and also because life changes fast as a motherfucker.

(4/5)

whereas when a guy is dead....he's dead. 

except for John McAfee. and MF DOOM. they're both probably somewhere in the BVI's.

when a guy is dead, u can look at all angles, take the good, leave the bad, and know that he's not get indicted at a P Diddy freak-off.

until they die, men can go several years, even decades, faking like turkey bacon the entire time. living a lie the entire time , sometimes out of misery, or necessity, or if it meant paying bills just unsure who they were they entire time.

or maybe fighting depression, or addiction, or one day u wake up and learn a guy u knew had enough of it all and unsubscribed from life.

and u see his face over the last 10 years, he was nmever in a bad mood. great life, wife, kids, not the one you'd expect. turns out he was fighting battles behind closed doors.

put another way, you can't really idolize them because the fog of war is too thick.

let the body get cold, u feel me?

(5/5)

so for principles and codes and "invisible mentors" and mental images of who u want to be, molds to grow into, books.

then, in person - aside from blood and day ones, circumstanctial friends, u want to find people who are like you.

ideally, you, but 10-20-30 years ahead of you on the track.

same gradient, in the quoted tweet below.

same personality type. someone in your career who can also be a mentor would be a slam dunk. but take what u can get. take multiple. have a Personal Board of Directors, that's 10 role models. 

a living role model doesn't have to be a saint - that's what the books are for.

and even there, you'll see that every great man has had some reprhensible side, God leaves no one excempt.

never made a perfect one, don't expect to find one.

and of course, before u determine who is worthy of your lavish devotion and praise, ask thyself:

are you a role model?

because if not, you got two options

you can lower ur expectations, u can raise ur integrity, and really, uc an do both at the same time

but the first is not only easier, but will increase ur love for ur fellow man.

“Blessed is he who expects nothing, for he shall never be disappointed.”   -Alexander Pope

quotedTweet.text:
life isn’t "choose your own adventure," but it IS “choose your own gradient”

at all times you can adjust the difficulty level, the slope, the extent to which u live outside ur comfort zone, in each 24-hour block that we are allotted.

you can either push yourself on a daily basis, or you can never push at all.

make it as steep or as flat as you'd like...the truth is that its going to be hard either way.

many ppl run it at flat, when counterintuitively, flat may be the worst option.

first, because inertia and ennui become the challenge. they substitute for the degrees of the gradient, and they cause far more gloom and despair than any steep climb.

second, because once you reach the end of life, you look back across the flat stretch of land -- the gradient prairie -- and u realize that u never did any of the things you said you'd do.

"Some people die at 25," they say, "and we don't bury them until 75."

so while u cant control others, and u never want to go around telling ppl how to live their life

what u CAN control is who u surround yourself with. and far more important than a lot of the other shit people prioritize... is finding ppl who play the same game, on the same wavelength, and who approach each 24-hour block on the same gradient that you do.
